subject: 465 Broadway Housing Code Hearing
overview: The Board held a hearing on persistent housing code violations at 465 Broadway, granted a grease trap variance for a nail salon, and discussed aligning tobacco license suspension language with state law.

items.title: October Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the October meeting.

items.title: New Member Introduction
items.summary: Welcomed Dina Caloggero to the Board of Health, noting her background in clinical laboratory science and public health.

items.title: Hearing for 465 Broadway Unit 4
items.summary: Reviewed six remaining housing code violations including pest activity, a disconnected radiator, and moisture issues that have been outstanding since September. The board ordered a follow-up inspection to verify that repairs currently in progress are completed before the tenant vacates in December.

items.title: Bliss Nails Grease Trap Variance
items.summary: Granted a grease trap variance for Bliss Nails at Station Landing because the business only serves prepackaged drinks and does not perform on-site cooking.

items.title: Tobacco Regulation 18 Amendment
items.summary: Discussed changing the local license suspension language from 'may' to 'shall' to ensure consistency with state law and remove enforcement ambiguity. The board requested a side-by-side comparison of state and local regulations for review at the next meeting.

items.title: Mobile Health and Community Announcements
items.summary: Announced the spring arrival of a Dana-Farber mammography van and the discontinuation of recurring Mass General Community Care Van visits. Staff also promoted an upcoming winter preparedness event and reported that over 500 flu and COVID-19 vaccinations have been administered this season.
